$comment: The Rite (design doc §7): each region's staged offering ritual and the Migration gate. Run 1 is authored here; runs 2+ come from the generator (Phase 4) using this as the template. A verse completes when chooseCount of its five slots are filled; slots are weighted so the spotlight crafts are the cheapest path. Resource offerings credit Renown at trade value; deed/specimen/fragment slots carry a fixed renownGrant, and so do resource slots offering unsellable MATERIALS (ingots, cordage — trade value is zero, the validator enforces the grant; values approximate amount x the material's notional input-derived worth). Verse lines live in dialogue.json (verses), verse sites in zones.json (verseSite). Quantities are first-pass — tune in Phase 3 against the §8 pacing targets.
$zoneRampNote: Goods amounts carry a GEOMETRIC zone ramp: x2.5 per zone order, anchored at zone 2 (zone 3 x2.5, 4 x6, 5 x15, 6 x40, 7 x100, rounded clean). The within-run power curve grows ~x2.5 per zone step — each later zone debuts against more stacked tool mults, more banked Verdure and more kith slots — so a flat ask collapses to seconds by the Hollows; tracking it holds every debut verse at roughly 20-40 min of its own node's production, and demandGrowth^m stacks on top as the real fold-over-fold stretch. Zones 1-2 are pinned by the hour-one pacing targets (verse 1 ~30 min) — do not ramp them. Material-slot renownGrants scale WITH their amounts (grant ~ amount x notional worth, the no-tax promise); deed/specimen/sketch slots stay authored — they price in taps and luck, and the generator scales only their grants. Zones 4-7 never play from this table (fold-gated past run 1) — their rows exist as the generator's value anchors. Ramp is model-derived 2026-07-31, NOT playtested — the run-3-to-run-6 sitting judges it.

generator.$comment: Run-2+ generator tuning (design §8: verseDemand(m) = baseQty · d^m, spotlight slots cheapest). demandGrowth is d; spotlight slots price at value × spotlightDiscount, off-spotlight at value × offSpotlightPremium. d is tuned against the fold's power ratio, not picked freely. A fold multiplies production by (1 + 0.02·Verdure) and Verdure is a square root of lifetime Renown, so that ratio starts near 3x across the first folds and settles at 1.10-1.15x from fold 7 on. d must sit just above the settled ratio: below it the gate stops gating, far above it the gate walls, because exponential demand always beats a power curve that is asymptotically linear. At the old 2.5 the twelfth fold asked ~1000x the wall-clock of the first; at 1.45 it asks ~2.5x, and folds 2-8 still run faster than the first (which is the prestige promise). spotlightDiscount / offSpotlightPremium are still first guesses.
generator.$breadthNote: The fold gate grows in BREADTH, not depth. Every second migration a verse asks for one more filled slot (chooseCount + m/chooseCountPerMigrations, capped at chooseCountMax), and the generator adds a goods slot in step so the choice margin the authored Rite has (5 slots, choose 3) never narrows. Breadth costs stationing, kith slots and map coverage rather than wait-time, and it is BOUNDED by how many slots a verse has — so unlike a quantity multiplier it can never outrun the player's power curve. The per-verse clamp in Rite.RequiredSlots is the real guarantee: a verse always keeps at least one slot of choice even where a lean zone gives the generator too few candidates to widen.
